sources.name: European Court of Auditors, Special report 17/2017: The Commission's intervention in the Greek financial crisis
ECB: Speech by Mario Draghi at the Global Investment Conference, London, 26 July 2012

steps.title: 2008: deficits on the periphery
text: Before the crisis, southern Europe bought far more than it sold. In 2008 Greece imported **$95.0 billion** of goods and exported $30.8 billion; its current-account deficit was **$51.3 billion**. Spain's was **$144 billion**.
Groups are split here, so each EU country is shown on its own, colored by its trade balance with the world.

steps.title: 2010: Greece needs a rescue
text: In May 2010 euro area governments and the IMF agreed a **€110 billion** support programme for Greece, the first of three.
Greece's goods imports fell from $95.0 billion in 2008 to **$61.4 billion** in 2012 (−35%). Its exports grew a little.

steps.title: Austerity and unemployment
text: Greece's economy shrank every year from 2009 to 2013, by as much as **9.9%** in 2011. Unemployment rose from 7.7% in 2008 to **27.7%** in 2013; in Spain from 11.2% to **26.1%**.
The map is colored by unemployment in 2013.

steps.title: From deficit to surplus
text: By 2013 the deficits were gone. Spain's current account went from −$144 billion in 2008 to **+$28.3 billion**, Italy's from −$65.0 billion to +$22.4 billion and Portugal's from −$31.2 billion to +$3.5 billion. Greece's deficit shrank to $5.0 billion.
Germany's surplus kept growing, from $206 billion to **$250 billion**.

steps.title: “Whatever it takes”
text: On 26 July 2012 ECB President Mario Draghi said the ECB was “ready to do whatever it takes to preserve the euro”.
Exports helped the recovery: Spain's goods exports rose from $221 billion in 2009 to **$306 billion** in 2013, above their 2008 level. Switch to Log to compare growth across countries.
